column1: # Deliberately not ported, and why.
# WHAT A ROW IN THIS FILE MAY SAY, set 2026-09-01 by the project owner and applied to every row below.
# 'cuML reaches it through a closed vendor library' is NOT a reason to refuse anything. It is a reason to
# WRITE IT OURSELVES, which this tree has already done for LU, potrf and trsm (cholesky/DERIVATION_MAP.tsv
# rows 18-19: 'none (cuSOLVER potrf is CLOSED)'). A row may say NOT YET IMPLEMENTED, with the portable route
# and the missing primitive named, or OUT OF SCOPE with a reason that is not 'theirs is closed', or
# DELIBERATELY DIVERGENT. Two rows below said the closed-library thing and are corrected in place.
# CORRECTION 2026-08-19: every 'raft linalg/detail/...' path below was wrong; these files live in cuML.
# NARROWED 2026-09-01: that correction was about the 25.08 pin (upstream/cuml, upstream/raft-v26.08.00's
# predecessor), where PCA and truncated SVD lived only in cuML. At the 26.08 pin RAFT DOES carry
# cpp/include/raft/linalg/detail/{pca,tsvd,rsvd}.cuh and cuML's pca.cu is a thin forward into
# raft::linalg::pca_fit. Rows below that cite a raft detail/ path were checked against
# upstream/raft-v26.08.00 and the path exists; the 2026-08-19 correction remains true of the paths it
# was written about, which were cuML's, and is not a licence to cite raft paths without opening them.
cuml cpp/src/tsvd/tsvd.cuh::calEig COV_EIG_DQ arm
column2: NOT YET IMPLEMENTED, AND IT IS THEIR DEFAULT
column3: divide-and-conquer, raft::linalg::eigDC -> cuSOLVER syevd. THIS IS THE ARM cuML's DISPATCH ACTUALLY TAKES: paramsTSVDTemplate::algorithm defaults to COV_EIG_DQ (cuml/cpp/include/cuml/decomposition/params.hpp:53) and the Python layer maps both 'auto' and 'full' onto it (pca.pyx:392-404). We ship the JACOBI arm, which is opt-in for them, and `PCA(svd_solver='jacobi')` now names it. CORRECTED 2026-09-01: this row used to end 'syevd is closed cuSOLVER so neither arm is portable'. That is the reasoning the owner's rule forbids and it is also false -- a divide-and-conquer symmetric eigensolver is as writable as the Jacobi we already wrote. It stays unimplemented for a different and better reason: it would be a SECOND numeric route to the SAME spectrum our device Jacobi already returns, so it buys a name and not a capability. If it is ever wanted, it is wanted for accuracy on a clustered spectrum, and that is the claim that would have to be measured first

column1: cuml cpp/src/tsvd/tsvd.cuh::calCompExpVarsSvd + raft linalg/detail/rsvd.cuh
column3: randomized SVD, `TruncatedSVD(algorithm='randomized')` and `PCA(svd_solver='randomized')`. ASSESSED 2026-09-01 against raft-v26.08.00/cpp/include/raft/linalg/detail/rsvd.cuh and it is REACHABLE, which is a change from what this row used to say. Their `randomized_svd` has TWO tails (:243 'either QR of B^T method, or eigendecompose BB^T method') and the SECOND one calls NO dense SVD at all: it reaches `raft::linalg::eigJacobi` (:364) plus `raft::matrix::sqrt` (:368), and eigJacobi is the very solver decomposition/checks/jacobi_eigh_device.mojo already substitutes for. The other pieces are a Gaussian sketch (`raft::random::normal`, :180 -- core/philox.mojo is the counter-based RNG and checks/numerics.mojo has the portable log/sqrt/trig a Box-Muller needs), gemms we have, and `raft::linalg::qrGetQ` (:198, :218, :241). THE ONE MISSING PRIMITIVE IS THAT QR: a tall-skinny Householder QR, bit-identical across three vendors, which is a lane the size of cholesky/'s potrf and not an afternoon. What is NOT a reason to skip it: cuSOLVER geqrf/orgqr being closed. NOT STARTED, no deviation number spent

column1: sklearn decomposition/_pca.py svd_solver='full' / 'arpack' (a dense SVD of X)
column3: ASSESSED 2026-09-01. FIRST, A CORRECTION TO WHAT THE PYTHON SURFACE USED TO CLAIM: it said 'full' is 'a different algorithm' in cuML, and in cuML it is not -- pca.pyx:394-395 maps BOTH 'auto' AND 'full' to Solver.COV_EIG_DQ, so for them the two names are one solver on the covariance. The name only means a dense SVD in scikit-learn (_pca.py:539-540 sends 'full' to _fit_full, which calls scipy.linalg.svd on the centered X), and scikit-learn's is the signature this class copies, so 'full' must mean the dense route or mean nothing. THE PORTABLE ROUTE IS R-SVD, which is what LAPACK does for a tall matrix anyway: Householder QR of the centered X, then a ONE-SIDED JACOBI SVD of the n_cols x n_cols R, which is a small in-block kernel very close in shape to jacobi_eigh_device.mojo and which this lane could carry. Its value over the shipped arm is real and is worth stating: forming X^T X squares the condition number and the dense route does not, which is the whole reason scikit-learn keeps 'full' beside 'covariance_eigh'. THE MISSING PRIMITIVE IS THE SAME ONE the randomized row names, a bit-identical tall-skinny QR. cuSOLVER gesvd/geqrf being closed is NOT the obstacle and is not offered as one

column1: cuml cpp/src/pca/pca.cuh::pcaFitTransform + ML::signFlip
column3: the U-based sign flip. Ours flips on V instead; see DERIVATION_MAP.tsv and the pca.mojo docstring for why, and note that cuML's pcaFit does not flip at all. DEVIATION 525 states our rule as a TOTAL order and pins it once in eig_and_truncate for both PCA and tSVD: largest-absolute-value entry, ties to the LOWEST index (cub::ArgMax's rule, cuML's own tsvd.cuh:160 loop, and np.argmax's), negate iff that entry is < 0.0 so a zero maximum of either sign never flips. Unconditional in BOTH numeric modes: it has been shipped since b495627, so gating it to IDENTICAL would move NUMERIC_FAST bits
